Franklin County Tax Deed Sales: A Safer Path to Property Ownership

If you’re looking for a smart way to invest in real estate, Franklin County, Virginia’s tax deed sales might be just what you need. When people fall behind on their property taxes, the county has the legal right to sell those properties at public auction. This gives investors like you the chance to buy property at a fraction of its market value.

Here’s everything you need to know to get started in Franklin County.

Introduction: Tax Deed Investing in Virginia

Virginia is a tax deed state. That means when you win a tax sale, you’re buying the property itself—not just the tax debt. These auctions can lead to big savings and strong profits, especially for buyers who do their homework.

Franklin County offers a structured process with clear rules and opportunities for high returns. Investors from across the country—and even outside the U.S.—can take part.

Important Tax Sale Information for Franklin County, VA

For full auction details, visit the Franklin County Tax Sale page, or contact the Franklin County Treasurer’s Office.

Fun Facts About Franklin County and Virginia

  • Over the past 10 years, Franklin County’s population has grown by just 2.36%, which is slower than Virginia’s 7.29% and the U.S. average of 6.23%.
  • The median home value in Franklin County is about $178,000. That’s well below the state median of $264,900 and the national median of $204,900.
  • Rent prices are also affordable, with a median rent of $724, compared to the state average of $1,202.
  • Virginia law does not provide a redemption period for tax deed sales, so once the court approves the sale, the property becomes yours.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

Things to See and Do:
Franklin County offers peaceful surroundings, outdoor parks, fishing spots, and historical museums. It’s also known for its scenic drives and lakeside views.

Transportation:
Major roads connect the county to Roanoke and other nearby cities. You’ll find easy access to highways and regional airports for travel and commuting.

Local Economy:
Agriculture, light manufacturing, retail, and small businesses play a big role in Franklin County’s economy. The area has a balanced pace of life with modest growth.

Community Life:
The community enjoys outdoor recreation, including hiking, boating, and festivals. The lifestyle here is relaxed and family-friendly.

Why Virginia Is a Great State for Tax Deed Investors

Virginia is considered one of the better states for real estate investing through tax sales. Here’s why:

  • No redemption period, which means you gain ownership faster.
  • You buy the property outright—not just the tax lien.
  • Auctions are open to all investors, including those from outside Virginia or outside the U.S.

Auction Process in Franklin County

Here’s a simple breakdown of how tax deed sales work in Franklin County:

  1. Auction Scheduled – When enough properties qualify, the county sets an auction date.
  2. Register to Bid – Some auctions require early registration. Check the county website for deadlines.
  3. Attend the Auction – Bidding takes place in person or online (depending on the sale).
  4. Pay the Deposit – If you win, you must immediately pay 25% of the final price (or $1,000—whichever is more).
  5. Pay the Balance – The remaining amount is due within 10 days.
  6. Court Approval – The sale must be confirmed by the court before the deed is issued.

Expected Returns and Investment Yield

Franklin County tax deed sales give you the chance to buy property below market value. Because there’s no redemption period, you avoid long holding times and gain ownership quickly. You may be able to resell, rent, or renovate these properties for a solid return.

International Investment Opportunities

Yes, international investors can participate in Virginia tax deed sales. Franklin County doesn’t restrict non-U.S. citizens from bidding, making this a global investment opportunity.

Why You Need to Do Your Research First

Before bidding on any property, make sure to:

  • Check the title – Are there other liens or legal issues?
  • Visit the property – You can do a drive-by inspection to see the location and surroundings.
  • Look into zoning rules – Is it residential, commercial, or landlocked?

Skipping research can result in unexpected costs or legal problems—so it’s important to know what you’re buying.

Buying Over-the-Counter (OTC) Tax Deeds

If no one buys a property during the auction, it may be available over the counter (OTC). These sales can be a great option:

  • No bidding competition
  • Fixed pricing
  • Easy paperwork

Check the Franklin County tax sale page or contact James W. Elliott for details on OTC opportunities.

Why Franklin County is a Smart Place to Invest

Here’s why Franklin County makes sense for tax deed investors:

  • Affordable property prices
  • Investor-friendly laws
  • Open to everyone—local and foreign buyers alike
  • Court oversight, which adds a layer of protection to your investment

Conclusion: Is Franklin County Worth the Investment?

If you’re looking for a low-risk way to invest in real estate, Franklin County’s tax deed sales could be a great option. The process is clear, properties are affordable, and you can gain full ownership quickly.

Just remember to do your research before jumping in.

Pro Tips for Tax Sale Investors

  • Register early and confirm auction dates on the county website.
  • Never bid on a property you haven’t at least seen from the outside.
  • Review each auction’s terms carefully—especially deposit rules and payment deadlines.
  • Set a budget and stick to it to avoid overpaying.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

Can anyone bid in Franklin County’s tax deed auctions?
Yes. Both local and out-of-state investors (even international ones) can participate.

How do I register for an auction?
Check the Franklin County Tax Sale page for deadlines and registration forms.

What happens if I win the bid but don’t pay?
You’ll likely lose your deposit, and the sale will be canceled.

Are these properties move-in ready?
Not always. Some need repairs or may be vacant land. Always inspect before bidding.

Can I buy properties after the auction?
Yes. Some unsold properties are available OTC—check with the Special Commissioner.
